newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin calls Russians to help reforms.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin calls Russians to help reforms.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin acknowledged popular dissatisfaction with economic hardship but told Russians on Thursday that their country was moving forward.
"I know how many justified grudges people have against...the authorities," Yeltsin said in a televised address marking the Russia Day national holiday.

"Despite the costs and difficulties of the transitional period, Russia is moving forward -- forward along the road of real political and economic transformations and, in doing this, overtaking many of its neighbours."

On this day in 1990, the Russian parliament chaired by Yeltsin proclaimed the sovereignty of the biggest Soviet republic in a step which the president's opponents say ultimately led to the collapse of the Soviet Union in late 1991.
Yeltsin on Thursday defended the parliament's decision.
"In the last seven years Russia has made a huge leap forward, we have chosen freedom and democracy," Itar-Tass news agency quoted him as saying at a state reception.

Heart problems, culminating in multiple bypass surgery last November, and pneumonia have kept Yeltsin out of the Kremlin for much of the time since he won his second four-year term in elections last summer.
But the 66-year-old Kremlin leader marked his recovery earlier this year with a series of bold steps clearly aimed at changing the face of Russia in the last years of his rule.
Facing strong public discontent over economic hardships and falling living standards, Yeltsin has brough young reformers into the cabinet and given them a free hand.
They have made clear they are ready to dump what remains of the Soviet system -- uncontrolled natural monopolies and a paternalistic welfare system.
"The economic refom started in 1992 these days has an absolutely unique historical chance to be completed," Itar-Tass news agency quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais as saying.
Addressing other public woes, Yeltsin has launched a new crusade against corruption and replaced the leadership of the defence ministry to push ahead the long delayed military reform.
Among other steps, he has struck a fragile peace deal with breakaway Chechnya, forged a loose union with neighbouring Belarus and moved to mend ties with Ukraine.
On Thursday, Russia's St Andrew's naval flag was raised on the ships of the Black Sea Fleet in its home base of Sevastopol on the Ukraine's Crimean peninsula.
That became possible after Russia and Ukraine resolved a long-running dispute over ownership of the former Soviet fleet.
"It is symbolic that it was on this day, June 12, that Russian St Andrew's flag was raised on the ships of the Black Sea Fleet," Yeltsin said in his television address.

"It is a symbol of the pride, honour and power of the Russian state and it is one more proof that we have no problems that we cannot solve. Russia is establishing itself firmly on its feet," he added.
